pass_a_gloss: Unit 9 open continues mid phrase from the kenosis: death, even cross death. Origen turns to saints’ love: Moses asks either forgiveness for the people or his own blotting from God’s book. Paul seeks the many’s benefit that they be saved, and could wish anathema from Christ for kin according to flesh; he prays anathema for others’ salvation. Fragment 52: tongues cease when conversation is mind to mind with the intended partner. Fragment 53: knowing and prophesying in part yield to the perfect; child speech, thought, and reckoning give way to manhood; present mirror riddle becomes face to face. Apparent progress here is childlike; when the perfect arrives and we reach perfect manhood we will hold adult knowledge, prophecy, and the vision the pure in heart receive. Fragment 54: the building gift outranks mere tongues unless interpretation also builds the church; high speech to self and God can leave the church unable to hear. Fragment 55 defines prophecy as worded knowledge of the unseen (world’s makeup, elements, times); teaching as instructional word for the many; revelation as mind exiting earthly things and dropping fleshly practice by God’s power; future knowledge may be called revelation loosely once proper senses are known. Fragment 56 shames uninterpreted tongues via flute, lyre, and trumpet analogies: no note distinction means unknown rhythm; unclear trumpet means no war readiness; uninterpreted tongue gives no distinction for understanding. Contemplative doctrines are flute and lyre (no ethics shown); exhortations to virtue are trumpet. Unclear Scripture (Leviticus sacrifices, Exodus tent) should not be read without clarifying exposition. Fragment 57: speaking into air still speaks in God; aerial powers hear though humans do not. Fragment 58 begins: many voice kinds in the world, none voiceless. The locked Greek is followed clause by clause in this sense gloss without adding foreign claims. pass_b_english: of death, even death on a cross. Come also to the saints; see Moses’ love: [[If you forgive them their sin, forgive; if not, blot me out of your book which you have written >> Bible:Exodus 32:32]]. And the apostle also says, [[just as I also please all in all things, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, that they may be saved >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:33]], and [[I could wish to be anathema from Christ for my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh >> Bible:Romans 9:3]]. He prays to be anathema from Christ for the salvation of others.
52 on [[1 Corinthians 13:8 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:8]]: “Whether tongues, they will cease.” [Origen:] Tongues will cease when I converse with mind to the one with whom I wish to speak.

53 on [[1 Corinthians 13:9–12 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:9-12]]: “For we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, then the partial will be done away. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, thought as a child, reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I did away with the things of the child. For now we see through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face.” [Origen:] The one who seems to advance here advances as among children; but when the perfect comes and we attain to a perfect man, then we will contain the things of men—knowledge and prophecy and the vision of God which the blessed will see because of purity of heart.

54 on [[1 Corinthians 14:5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:5]]: “For the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building.” [Origen:] The one who has the building gift is greater than the one who does not, inasmuch as the one with the building gift is more useful to the common good; but if the one speaking in tongues also has interpretation for building the church, the prophet is no longer greater. For sometimes he speaks high things, speaking to himself and to God, so that the church cannot hear.

55 on [[1 Corinthians 14:6 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:6]]: “But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you unless I speak to you either in revelation or in prophecy or in knowledge or in teaching?” [Origen:] Prophecy is knowledge that signifies the unseen through speech—knowledge of the world’s constitution and of the working of elements and times. Teaching is the instructional word distributed to the many. Revelation is when the mind goes outside earthly things and puts away every fleshly practice by God’s power; the one who obtains this has come into revelation. Perhaps also knowledge about future things can be called revelation; and one who has understood each term’s proper sense may use the names more loosely.

56 on [[1 Corinthians 14:7–9a >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:7-9]]: lifeless flute or lyre without distinction of notes; trumpet without clear call; tongues without clear speech. [Origen:] He wants to shame those who speak in a tongue into silence in church if there is no interpreter. Lifeless flute and lyre that give no distinction of musical notes are not known by what rhythm they played; the soldier does not arm for war unless the trumpet utters the voice that rouses to war; and those who speak in a tongue and do not interpret ought not to speak, as giving no distinction to the words for understanding. He called the doctrines of contemplation flute and lyre as showing nothing ethical, and those who urge toward virtue a trumpet. Hence one may say that the unclear parts of Scripture—such as the sacrifices in Leviticus and the tent in Exodus—should not be read unless someone clarifies their mind by exposition.

57 on [[1 Corinthians 14:9b >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:9]]: “For you will be speaking into the air.” [Origen:] The one who speaks in a tongue speaks in God; even if humans do not understand, still the powers about the air hear.
58 on [[1 Corinthians 14:10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:10]]: “There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is voiceless.”
